notes:
DraStic actually ships this time. 2.32.0 added it as a selectable DS engine but never
shipped the emulator itself, so choosing DraStic quietly ran melonDS instead. That is why
the pause menu still said melonDS. The emulator is in this update.

It brings docked dual screen with it: with the console docked, the DS top screen goes to
your TV and the touch screen goes to the console's own screen, touch included. Turn it on
per game under Docked screen mode. DraStic also runs at your docked resolution now instead
of dropping the TV to a stretched low-resolution mode, and its in-game menu pauses the game
instead of letting it run on behind the menu.

The performance overlay reports real numbers again. CPU and RAM looked like they dropped to
idle clocks mid game, which several of you reported. The overlay read the clock once a
second, and the CPU genuinely changes speed hundreds of times a second, so every reading was
a random snapshot. It now reports what the console actually averaged.

Also: battery level in the pause menu, a Game language setting for DS games, an option to
turn off the PS2 emulator's own pop-up notifications, and a clearer message when a port is
launched with no ROM installed. The hbmenu app updates properly now, so a console stuck on
an old NRO will get the current one.

Known rough edges: the docked right stick pointer on DS and 3DS still stutters, PS1 analog
controls still do not work in some games, and DS docked dual screen is new enough that
undocking mid game has not been tested by hand.
